correctness.rationale: A factor-by-marker-count proof reduces all possible non-letter Lyndon factors to three explicit run families. Their strict rotation criteria give (1), with no multiplicity collisions and with the all-one boundary. Four formal rational generating-function contributions prove (2); a dominant-gap inequality gives the unique maximum and three-unit spectral isolation. The Dirichlet-simplex reduction and six linear forms give exact limiting moments 19/24 and 37/45, and variance 563/2880. A standalone stdlib checker directly tested 5,985 weight-three words, 23,751 gap quadruples, the generating series through m=25, extrema, and rational moment arithmetic. Finite tests are corroboration, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected papers develop the general Lyndon-factor framework (Saari 2012) and unrestricted uniform-word averages and Christoffel extremals (Glen–Simpson–Smyth 2017). Neither states or entails the full conditional weight-three individual zero-gap classification, aggregate rational generating function, isolated top, or conditional variance coefficient. Actual exact-sequence, alias, and published mathematical record searches identified no covering result. Historical uniqueness is not claimed: unindexed special cases remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The number of distinct Lyndon factors is a standard primitive-rotation/string-complexity invariant. Conditional enumeration by a fixed number of markers is natural and differs from unrestricted sampling. The new statement completely classifies a nontrivial weight-three family, determines an all-length rational aggregate law, proves an isolated unique maximum with a sharp next-value gap, and gives a nondegenerate conditional limit distribution with explicit rational moment constants. The complete count and second-order fluctuations are substantive structural information beyond a textbook two-run check.
